A yidag — the truest form of the hungry ghost, belly swollen to bursting, throat thin as a needle — blocks the road. Not threateningly. It simply can't move. It wheezes:

"Please. Anything. Even a drop."

choices.text: Give it water

outcome.text: The water evaporates the moment it touches its throat. It weeps. You tried.

choices.text: Use white magic to ease its suffering

outcome.text: You temporarily widen its throat — just enough. It drinks for the first time in centuries, slowly, with its eyes closed. When it opens them, they're wet in a way that has nothing to do with the water.

choices.text: Ask how it came to this

outcome.text: A story of accumulated small greeds, none of them spectacular. It builds a picture of a life structured entirely around taking without giving — not evil, just narrow, for a very long time. The warning in the story is precise.

choices.text: You know what it is to want and not take.

outcome.text:
You sit down in front of it, which nobody does, and you do not offer it anything, which everybody does and which has never once worked.

What you offer instead is the observation that the wanting does not have to be obeyed. It is not cured. It is, for the first time in a very long while, spoken to.

choices.text: Help it let go

outcome_success.text: "There is nothing to drink here. There has never been anything to drink here. You can stop." It looks at you for a long time. Then, very slowly, it loosens its grip on existing. It dissolves, quietly.

outcome_failure.text: The suggestion that it could stop triggers something desperate. It attacks.

hg_smuggler_tunnel.title: The Smuggler's Tunnel
hg_smuggler_tunnel.text: A narrow tunnel entrance hidden behind a collapsed wall. Scratch marks on the stone suggest frequent use. From inside: voices, the clink of coin, the smell of something cooking.

choices.text: Enter cautiously
Announce yourself openly

outcome_success.text: A pause. Then: "Come in, then. Leave your paranoia at the door." Better prices for a customer who didn't sneak.

outcome_failure.text: "A spy." They don't wait to find out.

choices.text: Present yourself as a potential partner

outcome.text: You know the right words. They let you into the back room.

choices.text: Those scratches are not damage. They are a message.

outcome.text:
They are a message, in the sense that anything kept from most people is a message to the rest.

You read it: a count, a direction, and a warning about the third turning. All three prove accurate.

choices.text: Report them to the bone patrol

outcome.text: You find the nearest patrol and bring them back. The tunnel is raided. The Skeleton King's forces are grudgingly grateful.

hg_spirit_lanterns.title: The Lantern Procession
hg_spirit_lanterns.text: A line of ghostly lanterns floats through the darkness, each carried by an invisible hand. They move with purpose — a funeral procession of pure spirit, honoring someone important who died long ago. The procession repeats every night, endlessly.

choices.text: Walk alongside respectfully

outcome.text: You fall into step with the procession. The light is warm despite the cold. Something solemn and beautiful moves through you with it.

choices.text: Join the procession — carry a lantern

outcome.text: A lantern drifts into your hands. As you carry it, visions come — fragments of the honored dead's life, their work, their love for whatever is being mourned here. The procession ends at a marker stone. The lanterns settle. A long peace.

choices.text: Try to end the eternal repetition

outcome_success.text: You reach into the pattern of it and find where the loop closes. You open it. The lanterns flicker, then go still. The procession ends — truly ends. The darkness is darker for a moment, then easier.

outcome_failure.text: The pattern resists you. The procession blurs and stutters for a moment, then resumes its course as if nothing happened.

choices.text: Take one of the lanterns

outcome_success.text: The lantern comes away in your hands, warm and surprisingly heavy.

outcome_failure.text: The invisible hand does not let go. What was carrying the lantern turns its attention to you.

choices.text: Study the enchantment — understand what drives the loop

outcome.text:
The enchantment is a grief-loop — a mourning spell that has outlasted its caster by centuries, still running because no one cancelled it. The procession is real; the love in it is real. It just doesn't know it's allowed to stop.

You cannot dissolve it with enchantment alone, but now you understand its structure. The next person who walks beside these lanterns might be able to give it the permission it's been missing.

hg_gravedigger.title: The Gravedigger
hg_gravedigger.text:
A living man — actually alive — digs graves in the realm of the dead. He's been here so long he's forgotten how he arrived. He looks up as you approach without stopping his work.

"Someone's got to do it. The dead keep coming and the holes don't dig themselves."

choices.text: Help him dig

outcome.text: You work side by side in companionable quiet. At the end of it, he shares what he has — some food, some stories, a practical warmth that is rare in this realm.

choices.text: Ask how to leave this realm

outcome.text: "Couldn't tell you. Been trying myself." He leans on his shovel. "What I can tell you is: don't eat anything they offer. Don't go near the river after dark. And the Skeleton King's patrols are mostly reasonable, as long as you're doing something they can categorize."

choices.text: Offer to help him find his way home

outcome.text: He stops digging. Considers it for a long moment. "Who'd dig the graves?" He goes back to work. But something about him looks lighter after the question was asked.

choices.text: He is alive. Ask him how he is, before anything else.

outcome.text:
Nobody has asked him that. He gets asked what he is doing here, and how he got here, and whether he can be bought.

He leans on the spade for a while before answering, and the answer takes most of an hour and is worth the hour.

choices.text: Offer to trade — he's had interesting finds

outcome.text: He digs through a sack he keeps by the graveside. Things accumulate around graves. He has more than you'd expect, and most of it is in good condition.

hg_bone_library.title: The Bone Library
hg_bone_library.text:
Shelves of bone hold scrolls of dried skin. A bespectacled silver skeleton moves between them, filing and organizing with tireless precision. It turns at your approach.

"Knowledge doesn't decay. My work today may help somebody in a thousand years. What can I do for you?"

choices.text: Research a subject

outcome.text: The librarian pulls scrolls without hesitation, knowing exactly where everything is. What you find goes beyond what you expected to find.

choices.text: Ask about the realm's history

outcome.text: The librarian settles into it with obvious pleasure. The history of the hungry ghost realm is longer than you expected and stranger. You come away with the sense that this place has its own logic, older than any of the beings currently living in it.

choices.text: Offer a book from the living world

outcome.text: The librarian takes it with both hands, holding it carefully away from the bone shelves as if it might be infectious in the best possible way. "I have nothing like this. Nothing written after the living left." It opens the rare section.

choices.text: Steal a rare scroll

outcome_success.text: You find what you want and leave with it. The librarian doesn't notice.

outcome_failure.text: The librarian looks at you. Then at the scroll. Then at you again — not angry, just deeply, genuinely sad. You put it back.

choices.text: You are not leaving a library. Be reasonable.

outcome.text:
The silver skeleton adjusts its spectacles and produces, from somewhere, a second chair.

What you find in four hours is not what you were looking for and is considerably better: a name, an obligation, and where the obligation was last recorded.

choices.text: Do not read them. Index them.

outcome.text:
You go through the shelf-marks rather than the scrolls, which the librarian watches with mounting professional respect.

By evening you hold the shape of the whole collection, and the shape has a gap in it exactly where something was removed.

choices.text: Ask if they'd teach you a few things

outcome.text: "Well, I suppose. Why not." It pulls a selection of relevant scrolls and begins.

hg_swamp_hermit.title: The Hermit of the Mire
hg_swamp_hermit.text: Deep in the swamp, a rolang sits on a rock, fishing in toxic water with a line made of hair. It's the most peaceful undead you've ever seen. It has achieved something rare here — contentment.

choices.text: Sit and fish together

outcome.text: You sit in silence for a long time. Nothing bites. It doesn't seem to matter to either of you.

choices.text: Ask its secret

outcome.text: It doesn't look up from the water. "I stopped wanting." A long pause. "That's it. That's all there is."

choices.text: Offer what you're carrying

outcome.text: It shakes its head gently. "I have everything I need." It gestures at the toxic water, the dead fish, the grey sky. It means it.

choices.text: Disturb its peace — just to see

outcome.text: You consider it. Then the thought seems so ridiculous — there is so little peace in this realm and so much to disturb — that you simply leave. The faintest hint of hell clings to the idea.

hg_wandering_preta_event.title: The Wandering Preta
hg_wandering_preta_event.text:
A preta merchant dragging an enormous sack materializes from the grey. Despite being a hungry ghost, this one has channeled its craving into commerce with evident satisfaction.

"I can't eat, I can't drink, I can't sleep — but I CAN make a profit! Browse my wares?"

choices.text: Browse the wares
Ask what merchant life is like as a preta

outcome.text: "The margins are incredible since I no longer need to eat into them." A pause. "That's a joke. I can still make jokes." It delivers a ten-minute monologue on the economics of not needing to sleep, eat, or maintain any quality of life while operating a commercial enterprise.

choices.text: Offer it some of your food

outcome.text: It stares at the food for a long time. Then at you. "Nobody has done that in... a long time." It waves you away. "Take ten percent off whatever you buy. Consider it a professional courtesy."

choices.text: Rob it

outcome_success.text: Fast hands, fast feet. You're gone before it counts its stock.

outcome_failure.text: It screams loud enough to be heard across the wasteland. Apparently it has regulars.

choices.text: Make a joke about hunger for money

outcome.text: A wheeze that might be laughter. "Oh, that one's good. That one's actually good." It waves you toward the sack. "Take what you want. I'll give you the suffering-colleague discount."

hg_death_meditation.title: The Charnel Ground Meditation
hg_death_meditation.text: A flat stone among the bones, worn smooth by sitting. This is a practice site — you can feel it in the quality of the stillness around it. Confronting death directly. Not abstractly.

choices.text: Meditate on death fully

outcome.text: You sit and let the smell and the reality and the inevitability be present without distance. It is not pleasant and it is not supposed to be. When you rise, something has been processed that had been waiting to be processed for some time.

choices.text: Sit for a moment

outcome.text: A few minutes on the stone. The reality of the place presses in. You let it. Something small shifts.

choices.text: Study the bones academically

outcome.text: The collection here is unusual — varied, old, well-preserved by the dry air. You learn something about anatomy and something else, harder to name, about impermanence.

choices.text: You have sat in places like this before.

outcome.text:
The stone is worn smooth in the shape of people who have done exactly this, and you fit the shape.

What comes up is not fear, because that was dealt with some time ago. What comes up is the ordinary and much harder question of what to do tomorrow.

choices.text: Leave a prayer flag

outcome.text: You tie it to a bone and leave it fluttering. A small mark that someone was here and paid attention.

hg_toll_bridge.title: The Toll
hg_toll_bridge.text: Two massive skeletons in heavy armor flank a stone bridge. A sign lists prices that escalate from the merely unreasonable to the openly delusional. The skeletons seem bored.

choices.text: Pay the toll

outcome.text: They accept the coins without enthusiasm and step aside. Professional.

choices.text: Haggle

outcome_success.text: You work down through the price list methodically. They concede ground slowly, then all at once.

outcome_failure.text: They hold the line. The price goes up.

choices.text: Make them laugh

outcome_success.text: You hit something genuinely funny. One skeleton laughs so hard it falls apart at the waist, and is still clicking on the ground when you walk past.

outcome_failure.text: "Heard that one. Pay up."

choices.text: Read the sign properly. Signs like this always have a clause.

outcome.text:
There is a clause. There is always a clause, and you have spent enough of your life on the wrong side of one to find it inside a minute.

The toll applies to the living. Two of your party, on a technicality that the skeletons accept with visible irritation, are not paying it.

choices.text: Point out the economic flaws in the toll structure

outcome.text: You explain, briefly and with specific examples, why their pricing model is destroying long-term traffic revenue and creating a structural deficit. The skeletons stand very still for a long time. You walk past during this.

hg_realm_exit.title: The Border
hg_realm_exit.text: The air changes. Ahead, the grey wasteland of the hungry ghost realm gives way to something else. A boundary marker — a stone carved with the Wheel of Life — stands at the transition point. Behind you, the realm of craving. Ahead, the unknown.

choices.text: Cross without looking back

outcome.text: You step through. The grey lifts.

choices.text: Look back one last time

outcome.text: You turn. The realm reveals itself — not as horror, not as punishment, but as consequence. Everything here follows from something. The craving was always going somewhere. It came here. That clarity stays with you as you cross.

choices.text: Leave an offering at the boundary stone

outcome.text: For those still inside. You leave what you can spare and cross.

choices.text: Dedicate all merit gained here to the beings still suffering

outcome.text: You stand at the boundary and give it all away — every good thing earned in this realm, offered outward to those who couldn't earn it for themselves. The gesture costs you nothing you can measure. What it does is harder to name.

hg_mehr.title: The Eye in the Dark
hg_mehr.text: Something catches the thin light of the charnel grounds and throws it back — gold, steady, unblinking. Not an insect. Not a torch. An eye. Set in the face of a preserved woman standing knee-deep in black water, watching you with the patience of someone who has been here a long time.

choices.text: Call out to her

outcome.text: She answers. Dry, measured, without warmth or hostility. She answers your questions the way a stone does if you press your ear to it. She is not interested in traveling. You are not sufficiently interesting.

choices.text: Light a ritual flame — the old greeting of the Sun priesthood

outcome.text: The flame catches her attention in a way nothing else would. She straightens. Her golden eye moves before the other one does. 'Where did you learn that form?' She is already wading toward you before you finish answering.

choices.text: Ask about the prophecy — you have enough to read what she was reading

outcome.text: Her good eye narrows. The gold one does not move. 'That is the first intelligent question anyone has asked me in a very long time.' A pause. 'Come. Walk with me while I explain what it actually said.'

choices.text: Speak to her as an equal — not with reverence, not with wariness

outcome_success.text: She studies you for a long moment. 'You have the manner of someone who has survived things,' she says. 'I find that more persuasive than credentials.' She wades toward you.

outcome_failure.text: She looks at you the way she must have looked at the court before they threw her in the tar pit. 'I have heard every manner of introduction,' she says. 'Go.'

hg_choki.title: The Gathering
hg_choki.text: At the edge of a bog with no wind and no movement, a girl sits watching the water. She does not look up. She has been here long enough that moss has grown around where she sits. She is holding a bundle of forest plants that dried to nothing long ago.

choices.text: Leave her to the water

outcome.text: The bog is silent as you walk away. You don't hear her move.

choices.text: Touch the water beside her — let it speak for you

outcome.text: The water stirs slightly under your hand. She watches it. 'It was like that,' she says. 'One moment there was nothing. Then—' She trails off. Then: 'You are going somewhere. Can I come?'

choices.text: Ask her what she was gathering when the flood came

outcome.text: She finally looks up. Something in the question — the specificity of it, the acknowledgment of what she was doing when she left — gets through where comfort never would. She tells you everything she was carrying. She asks if you need a guide.

choices.text: Sit beside her without speaking — wait for her to acknowledge you

outcome_success.text: The silence stretches to an hour. Then two. Then she says: 'You're still here.' After another long while: 'Most people leave.' She looks at you sideways. 'Where are you going?'

outcome_failure.text: She doesn't acknowledge you. The waiting becomes its own kind of grief. You eventually stand and go.

hg_nangwa.title: The Unfinished Argument
hg_nangwa.text: In the collapsed shell of what was once a library — shelves of ash, scrolls of smoke — a barely-visible figure moves between the ruins. It is picking up nothing, reading nothing, but its lips are moving. Occasionally it stops, gestures at empty air, shakes its head, and starts again from the beginning.

choices.text: Watch him for a while, then leave

outcome.text: He doesn't notice you leave. The argument continues.

choices.text: Complete his sentence — you can see where the argument is going

outcome.text: He stops. Turns toward you with the most attention he has given anything in centuries. He seems to become slightly more present in the physical world as he focuses. 'Walk with me,' he says. 'I think better when I walk. Tell me if I have this right.'

choices.text: Reach toward him through space — make contact with the part of him that is still here

outcome.text: For a moment, genuine contact. He startles. Looks at his hands as if seeing them for the first time in a while. 'Oh,' he says. 'I have been quite far away.' He looks at you with new attention. 'Would you stay nearby? I find I concentrate better when someone is present.'

choices.text: Follow the argument — interrupt at the right moment

outcome_success.text: You catch the flaw and name it. He stops mid-gesture. 'Say that again.' You do. He is silent for a full minute. Then: 'I hadn't considered that approach.' A longer silence. 'Come with me while I think it through. I need a sounding board.'

outcome_failure.text: Your interjection breaks his concentration entirely. He dissipates for a moment, then reforms, looking confused and irritated. You have cost him hours of work.

hg_prashan.title: The Crossroads Question
hg_prashan.text: A vetala perches on a crumbling milestone, its mismatched layers of stolen cloth draped over a body it wears like a borrowed coat. It turns its head at your approach with the particular alertness of someone who has been waiting for exactly this. 'Ah,' it says. 'A traveler. I have a question for you.'

choices.text: Refuse to engage

outcome.text: 'As you like. You will be back. They always come back when they have had time to think of an answer.' It settles in to wait.

choices.text: Ask it a better question instead of answering

outcome.text: It goes very still. This has not happened before — or not for a very long time. 'You—' It stops. 'Where did you—' Stops again. Slowly, a smile spreads across a face not quite designed for it. 'All right. This is excellent. You will come with me. I insist.'

choices.text: Tell it a joke instead of answering

outcome.text: It blinks. Then, despite itself, makes a sound. Then another. 'That is — oh, that is terrible. That is genuinely terrible.' Its head is listing sideways with laughter. 'Come, I'll show you something better. I promise.'

choices.text: Answer the riddle

outcome_success.text: It tilts its head. Then further. Then further still, nearly upside down. 'Hmm.' A long pause. 'That is either a very good answer or a very bad one, and I cannot immediately tell which.' It straightens. 'I need to follow this further. Come with me.'

outcome_failure.text: 'No. That is the obvious answer. Everyone says that.' It gestures dismissively. 'Go away. Come back when you have thought more carefully.'

hg_nyingje.title: The Round
hg_nyingje.text: Among the ruins of a catacomb, a silver skeleton moves methodically from form to form — rolangs, dré, the occasional barely-present ghost. It is tending them. Binding wounds that will not heal, offering a hand to things that won't take it, reciting something under its breath to creatures that cannot hear. It does not seem to need an audience.

choices.text: Leave without disturbing her

outcome.text: She doesn't look up as you go. The recitation continues.

choices.text: Help her with her round — tend alongside her

outcome.text: You work in silence for a while. She watches your technique without comment. Then: 'You have been taught properly.' A pause. 'By whom?' By the time you finish answering, you are both walking. You realize later you agreed to travel together without either of you saying so directly.

choices.text: Sit in meditation nearby — make yourself a point of stillness in this place

outcome.text: She completes her round and comes back to where you are sitting. Waits. When you open your eyes, she is very close. 'You practice,' she says. It is not a question. A pause. 'I will walk with you for a while.'

choices.text: Ask her directly: will you travel with us?

outcome_success.text: She pauses in her work. Studies you with empty eye sockets that somehow convey careful attention. 'You are going further than here,' she says. 'There will be beings who need tending there too.' She finishes with her current patient, then stands. 'I will come.'

outcome_failure.text: 'I am needed here.' She returns to her work without hostility. It is simply true.

hg_khedrup.title: The Auspicious Count
hg_khedrup.text: On a flat rock carved with auspicious symbols, a preserved rolang sits in full meditation posture, counting beads with extraordinary precision. His lips move with sub-vocalized counts. Beside him, a pile of tally marks in the stone suggests he has been at this particular session for a very long time. He has the focused look of a man who is almost sure his formula is right.

choices.text: Leave him to his counting

outcome.text: The counting continues. The tally marks accumulate.

choices.text: Point out a flaw in his formula — you can see where the multiplier breaks down

outcome.text: His hand stops on the beads. He looks up for the first time. 'Show me.' You do. He studies it. Studies you. Then: 'I may need to revise my methodology. I would welcome a second opinion — going forward.'

choices.text: Examine his preserved state — make a technical observation

outcome.text: 'Copper oxide as the fixative?' He looks up sharply. 'How did you—' He examines his own hand, then back at you. 'What else can you tell?' The conversation goes on for some time. By the end he is standing. 'I should like to continue this. If you're traveling, I'll accompany you as far as convenient.'

choices.text: Wait for him to complete his count — do not interrupt

outcome_success.text: Three hours. Four. He reaches the end of his calculation, opens his eyes, and finds you there. 'You waited.' A pause. 'Most don't.' He consults his tallies. 'This is inconvenient. I will need to adjust for your presence in the calculation. Sit down. What is your birth star?'

outcome_failure.text: You shift at the wrong moment. He loses count, closes his eyes, and begins again from the beginning without acknowledging you.

hg_rasabhava.title: The Formula
hg_rasabhava.text: In a low-ceilinged catacomb chamber, a preserved zombie works steadily at a cluttered bench. Phials, powders, a bellows made of preserved lung. The formula on the stone tablet before him is enormously complex. He is at the part he always reaches before noticing something is wrong and starting over. He has not looked up.

choices.text: Leave him to it

outcome.text: He doesn't notice you leave. He's found something to check.

choices.text: Identify the phase where the formula breaks down

outcome.text: 'The stabilization phase — your catalyst ratio shifts at temperature.' He goes absolutely still. 'Say that again.' You do. He checks it three times. 'I have been wrong for forty-three years.' He closes his eyes. Opens them. 'I believe I need a different sort of problem. Will you have me?'

choices.text: Ask what he is trying to preserve and whether it can be summoned instead

outcome.text: He looks up for the first time. 'You're suggesting — instead of physical fixation, a binding of—' He sets down his tools. 'That would require a collaborator.' A pause. He looks at you properly. 'Come in. Close the door. I want to try something.'

choices.text: Read the formula over his shoulder — try to spot what keeps going wrong

outcome_success.text: You see it — a small error in the stabilization phase, invisible in isolation but fatal in combination. 'There,' you say. He looks. Silence. 'That can't be right. I've checked it six—' He checks it again. 'Oh.' The smallest, most deflated sound. Then: 'Are you traveling? I may want to get out of this room.'

outcome_failure.text: You can follow the general outline but the specifics are beyond you. He doesn't look up.

hg_durvasa.title: The Contained Curse
hg_durvasa.text: In a hollow beneath a collapsed stupa, a gyelpo sits within a circle of his own making — binding signs carved into the stone, faintly active. He is maintaining a careful stillness. Whatever is bound is inside him. He watches you approach with eyes that are doing a great deal of work to remain calm.

choices.text: Leave him to it — this is his problem

outcome.text: You feel his eyes on your back as you leave. The sigils continue to glow.

choices.text: Diffuse the bound energy through the air — disperse it gradually

outcome.text: It takes time. It takes all the steadiness you have. Gradually the sigils stop glowing. He slumps, then straightens. He looks at his hands, then at you. 'You have done this before,' he says. 'No,' you say. He considers this. 'Hm. I owe you a debt. How are you traveling?'

choices.text: Perform a proper reversal — unmake the binding through ceremony

outcome.text: The curse unwrites itself, step by step. He exhales for the first time in what sounds like a very long time. 'Thorough,' he says. 'Methodical. I appreciate methodical.' He stands slowly. 'Whoever taught you that taught you well. I find myself without current employment. Are you taking work?'

choices.text: Try to read the binding — understand what you are dealing with

outcome_success.text: A death-curse, reflected and internalized. He has been holding it in containment since it returned to him. 'How long?' you ask. He answers. You do not ask again. You sit across from him and begin talking through options. By the time the sigils fade, you are colleagues.

outcome_failure.text: You can see something is deeply wrong but not what. He watches you fail to understand with the patience of someone who has been sitting very still for a very long time.

hg_gomchen.title: The Contract Web
hg_gomchen.text: In a monastery that has somehow persisted in the charnel grounds — crumbling but still standing, its prayer flags bleached to grey — a gyelpo meditates in the central hall. Carved into every surface around him: contracts. Obligation clauses. Reciprocal bindings. The accumulated leverage of a long political career, frozen in stone. He sits in the center of it with his eyes slightly open.

choices.text: Leave him to his contracts

outcome.text: The hall is silent except for the slow erosion of stone.

choices.text: Dissolve the primary binding — force the keystone obligation apart

outcome.text: The stone cracks. The inscription flakes. He exhales slowly. 'I felt that.' The rest of the web loosens by degrees. He opens his eyes fully. 'You have just made me more dangerous. I hope you know what you are doing.' He stands, after effort. 'I owe you a debt. I prefer to pay them personally.'

choices.text: Read the obligations back to him — enumerate the full cost of what he is holding

outcome.text: You read them back slowly. Each one. He is very still. When you finish, the hall is quiet. 'I know,' he says. 'Say it again. Slower.' You do. When you finish the second time, something changes in his face. 'I have been very foolish,' he says quietly. 'Will you walk with me? I need to think outside these walls.'

choices.text: Study the contract web — try to find the obligation everything else depends on

outcome_success.text: You find it — a debt of precedence, buried under thirty layers of mutual obligation. You point to it without speaking. His eyes focus for the first time. 'You see it,' he says. 'No one has seen it.' A long pause. 'Then you are someone worth traveling with. Come.'

outcome_failure.text: The web is too complex. Everything connects to everything else. He watches you fail to find the thread without expression.

hg_bog_hermit.title: Bog Hermit
hg_bog_hermit.text:
A gaunt figure crouches in the reed beds, sorting through bundles of grey-green herbs with practiced hands. It is alive — or near enough to count. It looks up without alarm.

"You find herbs growing in the shade," it says by way of greeting, as if this explains everything. It holds up a sprig of something. "Helps with the rot. Mostly."

choices.text: Ask what the herbs are for

outcome.text: "Keep the living alive. Slow the dead down. Somewhere in between there's a tea that tastes almost good." It hands you a bundle without ceremony. You take it.

choices.text: Discuss the pharmacopoeia of the dead realm

outcome.text: You name what you recognise. The hermit corrects you once, with precision, then settles into a real conversation — the first, you suspect, it has had in some time. You leave knowing more than you arrived with.

choices.text: Sit with it a while — you have nowhere better to be

outcome.text: You sit. The hermit works. The bog makes its sounds. After a long silence it says: "Most people run through here." Another silence. "Thank you for not running."

choices.text: Ask if it trades

outcome.text: "I trade in knowledge, mostly. I already have everything else I need." It gestures at the grey sky, the toxic water, the rustling reeds. It seems to mean it. You move on.

hg_corpse_merchant.title: Corpse Merchant
hg_corpse_merchant.text:
A broad figure in a waxed coat stands over a cart heaped with cloth-wrapped bundles, sealed jars, and objects you decline to examine closely. Its face is partially masked. It does not smell good, but it has clearly made peace with this.

"Everything recovered in good condition," it says. "Relative condition. Relative good."

choices.text: Browse the goods
Ask where the goods come from

outcome.text: "The dead leave things behind. I collect them. Consider it a service." A pause. "To commerce. Also arguably to the dead. They weren't using it."

choices.text: Haggle — this is salvage, not retail

outcome.text: You explain the theory of salvage pricing. The merchant listens with professional attention and adjusts its margins. "Fair. You know the trade." The discount is modest but genuine.

choices.text: Pocket something while it looks away

outcome_success.text: The merchant turns to re-tie a bundle. In the gap, your hand moves. You're three paces gone before it straightens up. It doesn't seem to notice — or doesn't care. Possibly both.

outcome_failure.text: The merchant doesn't turn around. "I can smell the living," it says. "I can smell them reaching." It produces a heavy implement from the cart.

hg_preta_wail.title: The Wailing
hg_preta_wail.text: A chorus of voices rises from just beneath the waterline — hungry ghosts calling out in a language that is not quite sound. The words, if words they are, convey only need.

choices.text: Press on, ignoring the calls

outcome.text: Nothing reaches you. The voices fade behind you.

choices.text: Listen carefully — try to understand

outcome_success.text: One voice becomes distinct. A name. Something that mattered, once, somewhere.

outcome_failure.text: The need fills your mind for a moment. Hollow.

choices.text: Chant a mantra of compassion for them

outcome.text: The voices quiet, one by one. It doesn't solve anything. It might help anyway.

hg_will_o_wisp.title: Will-o'-Wisp
hg_will_o_wisp.text: A faint light dances ahead, moving just fast enough to stay out of reach. It has no face — just a glow, and an implied direction.

choices.text: Let it drift away

outcome.text: You watch it go. It doesn't look back.

choices.text: Follow it

outcome_success.text: It leads you to a dry patch of ground, then vanishes. Something is buried just beneath the surface.

outcome_failure.text: You step wrong. Bog, not ground. You pull yourself out soaked.

choices.text: Recognize it as a trapped spirit

outcome.text: You know this pattern. A soul caught between awareness and dissolution. You speak the syllable that releases it. It brightens, briefly, then goes out.

hg_swamp_spirit.title: Swamp Spirit
hg_swamp_spirit.text: A translucent figure stands ankle-deep in still water across a narrow channel. It watches you with the expression of someone who has forgotten where they were going.

choices.text: Wave and continue

outcome.text: It raises a hand in response. You don't look back.

choices.text: Speak to it gently — ask if it needs help

outcome_success.text: It doesn't answer in words, but something shifts. It presses a cold hand briefly to your forehead, then walks away into the mist.

outcome_failure.text: It stares at you for a long moment, then sinks slowly into the water. You're not sure what you said wrong.

choices.text: Offer guidance toward liberation

outcome.text: You know the practice for this. It takes most of an hour. The spirit becomes more present, then less, then gone — in the right direction.

hg_bone_raft.title: Bone Raft
hg_bone_raft.text: A crude raft of lashed femurs floats slowly past on the current. Something wrapped in waxed cloth sits in the middle. It's addressed to someone.

choices.text: Let it drift by

outcome.text: Whoever it's for, it's not you.

choices.text: Grab it before it floats out of reach

outcome_success.text: You snag it. The cloth is still dry inside.

outcome_failure.text: You lean too far. You get wet. The raft keeps going.

choices.text: Notice the name on the address — read it before it's gone

outcome.text: You can't retrieve it. But you read the name. It means something, even if you're not sure what yet.

hg_weeping_shrine.title: Weeping Shrine
hg_weeping_shrine.text: A small shrine on a mud-island, half-sunk. Water seeps continuously from the cracks in the stone — it has been weeping so long the ground beneath is stained dark.

choices.text: Make an offering and move on

outcome.text: The shrine accepts. The weeping continues.

choices.text: Meditate on what the shrine mourns

outcome_success.text: The grief becomes specific. A name, a cause, an old loss. Understanding doesn't fix it, but understanding tends to be useful.

outcome_failure.text: Grief doesn't always explain itself. You sit with it anyway.

choices.text: It is half-sunk and it is still a shrine.

outcome.text:
You wade out to it. This is unpleasant and takes some time and the party makes remarks.

What you find on the far side, above the waterline, is a carved instruction — brief, practical, and clearly meant for whoever cared enough to get that close.

choices.text: Perform a proper purification ceremony

outcome.text: The weeping slows, then stops — for the first time in however long. The shrine feels lighter. So do you.

hg_sacrifice_post.title: Sacrifice Post
hg_sacrifice_post.text: A wooden post driven into the mud, hung with trinkets, cloth strips, dried flowers. The offerings are from multiple eras — some ancient, some recent. Whatever this appeases, it is still being appeased.

choices.text: Add something small to the post

outcome.text: It costs you almost nothing.

choices.text: Try to identify what this protects against

outcome_success.text: You piece it together from the nature of the offerings. The swamp has teeth, and this is how the locals have been keeping them dull.

outcome_failure.text: Folk magic doesn't always leave notes. You make a small offering anyway.

choices.text: Take several of the more potent-looking charms

outcome.text: They're not yours to take, but they're functional.

hg_funeral_rites.title: Funeral Rites
hg_funeral_rites.text: A skeleton sits beside a crumbling grave, methodically arranging offerings — flowers long since turned to dust, fruit that is only the shape of fruit. It works without hurry, with complete attention.

choices.text: Don't disturb it

outcome.text: Some things should be left alone. You pass at a respectful distance.

choices.text: Watch what it is arranging — try to understand

outcome_success.text: You recognize the pattern. Old funeral rites, obscure but correct. Someone taught this skeleton well.

outcome_failure.text: You shift your weight. A branch snaps. The skeleton freezes. You hold your breath. Then it continues, ignoring you entirely.

choices.text: Kneel and help perform the rites correctly

outcome.text: It turns to look at you when you kneel. A long pause. Then it extends a handful of dust-flowers toward you, and together you finish the ceremony.

hg_memory_echo.title: Memory Echo
hg_memory_echo.text: A shimmer in the graveyard air, like heat haze — but it's cold here. For a moment you see a family at a meal. Vivid, fully real. Then gone, leaving only the smell of food that isn't there.

choices.text: Blink and move on

outcome.text: Some things are just residue of lives. You don't need to understand every one.

choices.text: Hold the vision — try to understand who they were

outcome_success.text: A life becomes briefly comprehensible. The attachment, the warmth, and what happened to it.

outcome_failure.text: The hunger in the image reaches you before the meaning does. You feel it in your chest for an hour.

choices.text: Study the echo's magical structure

outcome.text: A well-preserved echo. Whoever imprinted it was powerful in life, and thoroughly unresolved.

hg_skeleton_musician.title: Skeleton Musician
hg_skeleton_musician.text: A skeleton sits on a gravestone, playing a two-stringed instrument with surprising skill. The music is slow and strange and not entirely unpleasant. It stops when it notices you.

choices.text: Nod respectfully and pass

outcome.text: It watches you go. When you're far enough away, the music resumes.

choices.text: Play along, or try to match the melody

outcome_success.text: It tilts its head at you, then picks up the tempo. You manage to follow. For a few minutes, in a graveyard in the hungry ghost realm, something like music happens.

outcome_failure.text: Your contribution is not musically interesting. The skeleton watches you politely until you stop.

choices.text: Sing for the musician

outcome.text: It tilts its head at you, then picks up the tempo to match your voice. For a few minutes, in a graveyard in the hungry ghost realm, something like music happens.

choices.text: It is playing a form. Give it words.

outcome.text:
You put words to what it is playing, roughly and out of metre, and it stops dead for the length of a breath before picking the line back up underneath your voice.

You get through four verses. It has not had a singer in a very long time.

choices.text: Tell a joke

outcome.text: It makes no sound. But the jaw moves, and the ribcage shakes, and the instrument ends up upright and the musician hunched over it in a posture that can only be described as helpless.

hg_dust_storm.title: Dust Storm
hg_dust_storm.text: A wall of bone-dry grit sweeps across the graveyard with no warning. There's nowhere to shelter. You're going to take this one.

choices.text: Push through

outcome.text: You bow your head and walk. It gets in everywhere.

choices.text: Brace against it — or dodge the worst of it

outcome_success.text: You turn your back, cover your face, wait it out. It passes.

outcome_failure.text: It's worse than you thought.

choices.text: Raise a wind-break with earth magic

outcome.text: A low ridge of packed earth takes the worst of it. You emerge into clear air already reforming your thoughts about dry graveyards.

hg_dancing_dead.title: The Dancing Dead
hg_dancing_dead.text: A ring of corpses dances in perfect silence around an empty throne. Their movements are stiff but coordinated, as if memory persists where intention does not. They do not appear to notice you.

choices.text: Slip past the outer edge carefully

outcome.text: Whatever they are celebrating, or mourning, continues without you.

choices.text: Join the ring — dance with them

outcome_success.text: Your body finds the rhythm. For a moment you are part of something very old and very strange. When the dance ends, you are on the other side of the ring.

outcome_failure.text: You misstep. The ring shifts. They look at you all at once. Then, somehow worse, they resume — leaving you outside it.

choices.text: Let them have it. Watch properly.

outcome.text:
They are dancing around an absence and they are doing it in total silence and they have clearly been doing it a long time.

You watch it through rather than past, which nobody has done, and at the end one of them bows to you specifically.

choices.text: Recognize the ceremony and complete your part

outcome.text: This is a specific ceremony. You've seen fragments of it. You take the empty throne, perform your part. When you rise, the dance resolves — the figures slow, then still, with something like satisfaction.

hg_spirit_fire.title: Spirit Fires
hg_spirit_fire.text: Three fires burn without fuel at the edge of the charnel grounds. One is pale blue, one is deep green, one is a colour that doesn't have a name. None of them give off heat.

choices.text: Walk around them

outcome.text: They seem to watch you go — or seem to.

choices.text: Approach and study them

outcome_success.text: Each one is a distinct consciousness, in the earliest stage of what might become a ghost or might become something else. You learn something from how they burn.

outcome_failure.text: The nameless-coloured one flares. The heat is not physical. You step back.

choices.text: Understand their elemental nature

outcome.text: Three elements, one process. You spend time with each one, and each one teaches you something.

hg_charnel_feast.title: Charnel Feast
hg_charnel_feast.text: A long table laid out in the open, covered in a feast that looks perfect and smells wrong. Seated pretas reach for food endlessly — it passes through without satisfying anything. The table is infinite. The hunger is infinite. Neither notices you standing at the edge.

choices.text: Turn away quickly

outcome.text: The right call.

choices.text: Eat anyway — you're hungry, and it looks real enough

outcome_success.text: It's real enough. Strange but real. It sits wrong for an hour, then doesn't.

outcome_failure.text: You understand, briefly and completely, what it is like to need something and have it provide nothing at all.

choices.text: Sit with the nature of what you're seeing

outcome.text: You observe the feast without hunger. The pretas slow, one by one, and watch you — the strange creature at the edge of the table who is not reaching. Something about this interests them.

choices.text: You have been hungrier than this on purpose.

outcome.text:
You look at the table the way you look at any table, which is to say briefly.

Whatever laid it was counting on the wanting, and there is not enough of that in you to work with. The hall loses interest and the food stops being convincing halfway down the table.

choices.text: You can tell from here that the lamb is done properly.

outcome.text:
You can. That is the trouble — it is not a general temptation, it is a specific and extremely well-observed one, and something went to the effort of knowing what you would want.

You eat one mouthful before the party gets you away from the table. One is enough to be unwell for a day.

choices.text: Pocket the gold candleholders — they look real

outcome.text: They are real. Everything solid about this table is real.

hg_sigh_of_relief.title: A Sigh of Relief
hg_sigh_of_relief.text: A small cairn with a folded cloth on top. Written in a careful hand: "You are not as lost as you feel."

choices.text: Read it. Move on.

outcome.text: You are not as lost as you feel.

hg_black_lodge.title: Black Lodge
hg_black_lodge.text: A mound of bones marks the entrance, a khatvanga hung with a skull and streaming black silk. As you enter, the darkness swallows sound. Something in the corner shifts — it may not be fully alive. A slow turn. A waiting smile.

choices.text: Ask to learn

outcome.text: The movement stills. A bony hand gestures to a list scratched into the wall. Spells. Prices. No explanation offered.

choices.text: Say nothing at the door. That is the password.

outcome.text: It is. You are inside before you have decided whether you wanted to be, and what is discussed there is not written down anywhere, including here.

choices.text: Back out

outcome.text: You step back into the pale light. The khatvanga watches you leave.

hg_yogini_circle.title: Circle of the Yoginis
hg_yogini_circle.text: Sixty-four forms carved into standing bones form a perfect ring on the charnel ground. The earth inside is worn smooth by countless ritual footprints. A low humming comes from the center — women's voices, or something passing for them.

choices.text: Enter the circle

outcome.text: One of the sisters turns. No words — a gesture toward the center of the ring. What do you need?

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You back away slowly. The humming follows you longer than it should.

hg_crossroads_stupa.title: Crossroads Stupa
hg_crossroads_stupa.text: At the intersection of the ancient paths, a stupa rises from layers of offerings — skulls, prayer flags, bones wrapped in cloth. Juniper smoke and the smell of old offerings drift on the wind. A practitioner crouches behind the stupa, neither fully alive nor fully dead.

choices.text: Approach the stupa

outcome.text: The figure looks up. The crossroads is the right place for calling back what is lost. The price is gold.

choices.text: Observe from a distance

outcome.text: You watch the butter lamps flicker in the wind, then walk on. Some things are better left undisturbed.

hg_hidden_gompa.title: Hidden Gompa
hg_hidden_gompa.text: A small monastery sits undisturbed between the burial grounds, its walls marked with painted eyes that seem to follow you. The monks here practice for the benefit of all beings caught between lives. The ground vibrates faintly with their prayers.

choices.text: Knock and ask to enter

outcome.text: After a long pause, the door opens. A monk gestures you inside and names what can be taught here — and the price.

choices.text: Don't disturb them

outcome.text: You walk past without knocking. The painted eyes seem to close behind you.

hg_mirror_lake.title: Mirror Lake
hg_mirror_lake.text: The surface of the lake is perfectly still, reflecting not the sky above but something else — other realms, other moments, faces that do not look back when you stare. Practitioners sit at its edge, meditating on what the water reveals.

choices.text: Sit and listen

outcome.text: A practitioner meets your eyes in the reflection before turning around. They can teach what the lake teaches. The water makes everything a fair price.

choices.text: Walk away from the mirage

outcome.text: You step back from the water's edge. The reflection holds your shape a moment longer, then dissolves.

hg_sacred_grove.title: Sacred Grove
hg_sacred_grove.text: A stand of ancient trees whose roots grow through charnel earth. The branches are hung with offerings of food — the hungry ghosts who press at the edge of the grove can smell them but cannot eat. Practitioners move among the roots, speaking to both the living and the dead.

choices.text: Approach the practitioners

outcome.text: One of the practitioners turns. She names what can be taught here, and then the price. Gold is gold in every realm.

choices.text: Leave them to it

outcome.text: You walk on. The smell of offerings follows you through the trees.

hg_temple_of_the_naga.title: Temple of the Naga
hg_temple_of_the_naga.text: A low temple built around a black-water pool. The nagas who dwell in such pools are guardians of the dead, and their human followers leave milk offerings at the water's edge. A practitioner sits cross-legged on the stone, eyes closed, lips moving.

choices.text: Ask about their teachings

outcome.text: The practitioner opens her eyes. She names the spells the nagas have permitted to be taught here, and the price. It is not cheap.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the offerings undisturbed. The pool surface ripples once as you go.

hg_mercenary_guild.title: Mercenary Guild
hg_mercenary_guild.text: A walled compound marked with the crossed-bone sigil of the guild. Skeletal warriors and half-dead fighters linger between contracts, sharpening weapons they barely need to use anymore.

choices.text: Enter the guild

outcome.text: The guildmaster looks you over without interest. Weapons, armor, contracts — name what you need.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the compound to its dead-eyed inhabitants.

hg_peddler_graveyard.title: Wandering Preta
hg_peddler_graveyard.text: A preta wanders between the grave markers, its distended belly dragging, desperate hands clutching bundles of goods. It will trade anything for food — though it can never eat enough to be satisfied.

choices.text: Trade with the preta

outcome.text: The preta's needle-thin neck cranes toward you, eyes fixed on your pack. It lays its goods on a grave marker and waits.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You give the preta a wide berth. It watches you go with hollow, hungry eyes.

hg_peddler_swamp.title: Wandering Preta
hg_peddler_swamp.text: A preta rises from the mist at the water's edge, its needle-thin neck craning as it senses your approach. Desperate hands clutch wares salvaged from the swamp floor. It will trade anything for food.

choices.text: Trade with the preta

outcome.text: The preta spreads its goods on a half-submerged log and regards you with hollow, hopeful eyes.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave it to the mist. Its eyes follow you until the fog closes in.

hg_teahouse_charnel.title: Charnel Teahouse
hg_teahouse_charnel.text: A lantern glows faintly above a low doorway carved into a wall of stacked bone. Inside, a quiet figure brews tea from dried flowers that grow only on graves. The dead do not drink, but the living are welcome.

choices.text: Step inside

outcome.text: The figure pours without looking up. You can rest here — if you can afford it.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the lantern light behind. The scent of grave-flowers follows you a while.

hg_teahouse_graveyard.title: Graveyard Teahouse
hg_teahouse_graveyard.text: A small dwelling built into the side of an old burial mound, its entrance marked with a hanging lantern and a painted sign no longer legible. Someone has been serving tea here for a very long time.

choices.text: Step inside

outcome.text: The host gestures to a low table. The tea is bitter and dark. You can rest here — if you can afford it.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the mound behind. The lantern swings in a wind you can't feel.

hg_teahouse_swamp.title: Swamp Teahouse
hg_teahouse_swamp.text: A teahouse built on stilts above the swamp water, its light the only warmth for miles. A rope bridge leads to the door. Someone is already watching you from the window.

choices.text: Cross the bridge

outcome.text: The host sets a cup on the table before you sit. You can rest here — if you can afford it.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the light behind. The swamp closes around you.

hg_town_magic.title: Town
hg_town_magic.text: A settlement where more windows glow than can be explained by candlelight. Strange smells drift from the apothecary. A practitioner argues with a vetala outside the library, and neither seems to have the better of it.

choices.text: Enter the town

outcome.text: You find the market square. The odd merchants eye you with professional interest.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the scholars to their arguments. The strange lights fade behind you.

hg_town_supplies.title: Town
hg_town_supplies.text: A trading post built among the graves, supplies scavenged from the dead and traded among the half-living. The market is quiet but well-stocked — necessity makes practical merchants of everyone here.

choices.text: Enter the town

outcome.text: You push through to the market. Traders call out their wares in dry, patient voices.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You skirt the settlement and keep moving.

hg_town_weapons.title: Town
hg_town_weapons.text: A fortified compound where warriors trade blades and bones. The biggest building is an armory. Someone is always sharpening something, and the sound of whetstones never stops.

choices.text: Enter the town

outcome.text: You push through the gate. The armorer looks up from their work.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You skirt the compound and keep moving.

hg_veterans_camp.title: Veterans' Camp
hg_veterans_camp.text: A camp of battle-scarred fighters who never left the ghost realm. Their fire has been burning since they arrived — they stopped counting how long ago. They still trade in the tools of their old trade.

choices.text: Approach the camp

outcome.text: A veteran looks up from the fire. Old fighters make fair merchants — they know what things are worth.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the veterans to their fire. It will still be burning when you pass this way again.

hg_shadow_market.title: Shadow Market
hg_shadow_market.text: A market that appears only between the grave stones, visible only to those who know how to look. The stalls are draped in dark cloth and the merchants keep their faces in shadow. Everything here was obtained quietly.

choices.text: Browse the stalls

outcome.text: A shadowed hand gestures you deeper into the market. No questions asked, no names given.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You step back. The market seems to thin and vanish between blinks.

hg_shadow_peddler.title: Shadow Peddler
hg_shadow_peddler.text: A hunched figure steps from behind a grave marker, face obscured beneath a ragged hood. Its voice is barely a whisper but its goods are real enough — things it has acquired in ways it declines to explain.

choices.text: See what it has

outcome.text: The figure spreads its goods on the grave stone between you. It wants food more than gold.

choices.text: Keep moving

outcome.text: You walk past without stopping. The figure watches you go, then is gone.

hg_boss_insatiable_king.title: The Insatiable King
hg_boss_insatiable_king.text:
He sits on a throne of fused bone before the Realm Gate, a mountain of a preta — belly vast as a granary, throat thin as a needle. A thousand offering bowls lie scattered around him, every one licked clean and none of them enough.

"More," he says, and the word carries the weight of centuries. "Everything that passes this gate feeds me first. Wealth. Blood. Memory. What have you brought the King of Hunger?"

choices.text: Give him nothing — draw your weapon
Lay out a feast from your own stores before the fight

outcome.text: He devours everything in moments — and for one heartbeat his eyes close, almost peaceful. When they open, the hunger is back, but slower. Heavier. He rises to fight without his court.

choices.text: Speak the sutra of the open hand — hunger ends where giving begins

outcome.text: The words land like rain on a fire that has burned for ten thousand years. His courtiers dissolve, wailing. The King alone remains, diminished, weeping — and still he attacks, because he no longer knows how to do anything else.

choices.text: Sit with him. Ask what he was, before the hunger

outcome.text:
The question stops him like a blade. Slowly, haltingly, he remembers: a rich man who buried grain while his village starved, who died counting. You sit with the memory until he can hold it himself.

When he finally weeps, the tears are ordinary and human. The throne of bone crumbles. Where the King sat there is only an old man's shadow, bowing once before it fades. The gate stands open.

hg_swamp_warden.title: Swamp Warden
hg_swamp_warden.text:
The only dry crossing through the wall of thorn and mire is watched. A rolang ancient stands waist-deep in the black water, preserved by centuries of swamp tannin, carrion worms moving beneath its skin like slow thoughts.

It raises one dripping arm and points — not at you, but at the toll stone beside the path, hollowed like a begging bowl.

choices.text: Cut it down and force the crossing
Fill the toll stone with food and pass

outcome.text: The worms boil out of the warden's body to swarm the offering. While the ancient stands hollowed and swaying, you walk the causeway unopposed.

choices.text: Perform the rites that should have been spoken over this corpse

outcome.text: You speak the old words and the warden goes very still. The worms leave it, one by one, sliding into the water. What remains is only a dead man, finally allowed to be dead, toppling softly into the reeds. The crossing is yours.

choices.text: Wade through the deep mire, out of its reach

outcome_success.text: Chest-deep in rot, leeches at your ankles, you haul yourselves through the mire and up the far bank, shaking but past.

outcome_failure.text: The mud holds you fast — and the warden comes wading.

hg_bone_gate_keeper.title: Bone Gate Keeper
hg_bone_gate_keeper.text:
The pass through the ossuary wall runs beneath an arch of ten thousand fused skulls. Before it stands a skeleton formation in ancient parade order — warriors, archers, and at their center a bone horror wearing the rusted regalia of a gate captain.

Its jaw grinds open: "State. Your. Dead."

choices.text: Break the formation
Name your dead, honestly, one by one

outcome.text: You speak the names — companions lost, enemies slain, the lives that ended so you could stand here. The captain's skull tilts with each one, counting. When you finish, the formation parts with a sound like dry applause.

choices.text: Command them in the tongue of the dead

outcome.text: Your word of command cracks across the pass like a whip. The formation snaps to attention — and holds it, rigid, as you walk through their ranks. The captain's eye sockets track you the whole way.

choices.text: Return the salute and inspect the honor guard

outcome.text: You walk the line like a visiting general. Halfway down the rank, the captain decides you are worth testing — but formation discipline binds most of its troops to their posts.

hg_zombie_horde.title: Zombie Horde
hg_zombie_horde.text:
They come out of the reeds in ones and twos and then in dozens — bog zombies, waterlogged and patient, drawn by whatever it is the living give off that the dead can smell.

There is no line to hold. There is only the direction with fewest of them in it.

choices.text: Cut a path through
Go low into the reeds and let them pass over you

outcome_success.text: Face-down in black water breathing through a reed while a hundred waterlogged feet go past inches from your ribs. It takes forty minutes. Nobody coughs. That is the whole achievement and it is enormous.

outcome_failure.text: Somebody's lungs give out. A head turns. Then all of them turn.

choices.text: Set the marsh gas alight behind you

outcome.text: There is more methane over this bog than anyone should stand in. You touch it off from the far side and the whole flat goes up in a low blue sheet. The horde does not so much burn as simply stop, mid-step, and keep standing there while the fire takes them. You are well clear. You watch longer than you meant to.

choices.text: Sever what is holding them upright

outcome.text: Rolang are not animate by their own will — something keeps them walking, and it is thin here. You speak the release across the whole flat at once and the horde goes down in a long ragged wave, like a field of wheat. In the silence afterwards the swamp sounds almost ordinary.

hg_swamp_toll.title: Zombie Toll
hg_swamp_toll.text:
The causeway is the only dry ground for a mile, and four bog zombies stand across it in a row. They are not shambling. They are *waiting* — arranged, deliberate, with the stillness of a posted guard.

One of them holds out a swollen hand, palm up. It has been taught to do this.

choices.text: Break the line
Put something in the hand

outcome.text: The fingers close. The four of them step aside in unison and resume waiting, facing the way you came. Somewhere in this swamp is whoever trained them, and you find you would rather not meet them.

choices.text: Follow the training back to whoever set this up

outcome.text: The zombies are facing the causeway, but their heels are aligned to a stand of dead willow forty paces off. There is a rolang in it, very old, very still, running a toll booth in a swamp with four corpses and infinite patience. You negotiate directly. It turns out to be reasonable, and lonely, and it waives the fee for conversation.

choices.text: Four zombies and a causeway. Do the arithmetic out loud.

outcome.text:
You establish, at length, that the causeway is not theirs, that no work has been done to maintain it, and that the toll has no basis of any kind.

The zombies are not equipped for this argument. Two of them wander off during it.

choices.text: Pay with something that is not money

outcome.text: You press a flat river stone into the swollen palm with great ceremony. The fingers close on it. Whatever instruction these four are running does not include an assay step. They step aside. You cross the causeway feeling both clever and slightly cheap.

hg_rotting_bridge.title: Rotting Bridge
hg_rotting_bridge.text:
The bridge is the only crossing for miles and it has been rotting for longer than that. Half the planks are gone; the rest are the colour of old cheese. Beneath it, the channel runs deep and black and busy.

Someone has scratched a warning into the post. The scratching is also rotten.

choices.text: Cross one at a time, testing every board

outcome_success.text: Four crossings, four held breaths, one plank that goes into the water without you. Everyone across.

outcome_failure.text: The board does not creak first. One moment there is a bridge and the next there is black water and a great deal of movement in it.

choices.text: Rebuild the span properly before anyone sets foot on it

outcome.text: You cut and set new stringers, deck it in salvaged planks, and lash the whole thing to the surviving piles. It takes four hours and a quantity of scrap. When you finish, it is the only sound structure you have seen in this realm — and it will still be here for whoever comes next, which is a strange thing to care about in a place like this.

choices.text: Find where the channel shallows and ford it

outcome.text: Bridges exist where the crossing is hard. Two hundred paces upstream the channel spreads over a gravel bar and is thigh-deep and boring. You get wet to the hip and nothing tries to eat anyone.

choices.text: Not worth it — go the long way

outcome.text: Most of a day added to the journey and every member of the party privately relieved.

hg_lost_traveler_swamp.title: Lost Traveler
hg_lost_traveler_swamp.text:
He is sitting on his pack in six inches of water, and he is alive — properly alive, breathing, shivering, sunburnt on one side of his face from a sun that does not shine here.

"I've been walking in a circle," he says, with the terrible calm of someone who worked this out some time ago. "I keep finding my own footprints. I've stopped following them."

choices.text: Take him with you as far as the next dry ground

outcome.text: He talks for the first hour and then stops, and the silence afterwards is better. At the treeline he shakes everyone's hand formally, one at a time, and walks off south. You do not find out whether he makes it.

choices.text: Give him food and directions

outcome.text: He eats too fast and apologises for it. The directions he repeats back to you three times, getting them right on the third.

choices.text: Ask how a living man got into the realm of the dead

outcome.text: He does not know, and the not-knowing is the whole horror of it. But in the telling he mentions a doorway in a hillside, a smell of jasmine, and a woman who asked him to carry something. You write down everything he says. Some of it will matter later.

choices.text: He is not lost. He is somewhere he does not want to be.

outcome.text:
Lost is a thing you can fix with directions. This is the other thing, and you recognise it because you are carrying a version of it yourself.

You do not give him directions. You sit in the water next to him for a while, and then you both get up.

choices.text: Break whatever is turning him in a circle

outcome.text: The loop is real and it is thin — a fold in the swamp about a mile across that returns everything to its own footprints. You cut it. The change is not visible; it is simply that the horizon means something now. He starts crying, which he seems as surprised by as you are.

hg_sunken_village.title: Sunken Village
hg_sunken_village.text:
Roof-ridges break the water in rows. A whole village went under here and did not go anywhere else — the water simply arrived and stayed, and the village kept its shape beneath it.

In the shallows at the edge, a cooking pot sits on its stones, upright, full of black water.

choices.text: Leave it under the water

outcome.text: The roof-ridges are still visible a long way down the road, whenever you look back.

choices.text: Work the shallow houses

outcome.text: Waist-deep through what used to be doorways. Cookware, tools, a strongbox nobody had time for.

choices.text: Dive the headman's house at the centre

outcome_success.text: Three dives. The third one gets the box out of the rafters where somebody put it when the water was already at the door.

outcome_failure.text: Something in the rafters is not a rafter, and it has been waiting in the dark of that room for a very long time.

choices.text: Say the water-rites over the whole village

outcome.text: You stand in the shallows and name the village — you do not know its name, so you name it by what it was: a place where people cooked and argued and slept. The water does not change. But when you go through the houses afterwards nothing objects, and in the headman's rafters you find what was hidden there, and it comes away easily.

hg_flooded_crypt.title: Flooded Crypt
hg_flooded_crypt.text:
Stone steps go down into standing water. Whatever this was built to hold has been below the waterline for centuries, and the swamp has been patiently filling it the entire time.

The first two feet of the stair are slick with something that is not algae.

choices.text: Some doors stay shut

outcome.text: You go back up into the grey daylight, which is not much, but is more than what is down there.

choices.text: Wade in with torches

outcome_success.text: Chest-deep, torch held over your head, through three chambers of grave-goods that nobody has been able to reach since the water came. Cold beyond describing. Worth it.

outcome_failure.text: The torch goes out in the second chamber. In the dark, something that has been standing in this water for four hundred years turns to face the sound of you.

choices.text: Part the water and walk in dry

outcome.text: You push the water back down the stair and hold it there, and walk into a crypt that has not been dry since its builders sealed it. The sentinel in the third chamber is standing exactly where it was posted. It does not attack. It looks at the dry floor for a long moment and then, apparently satisfied that its watch is finally over, sits down and stops.

choices.text: Read the seals on the doorway before opening anything

outcome.text: The seals are not protective. They are a *containment*, and the water is part of it — whoever flooded this crypt did it on purpose and did it well. You take what is in the entry chamber, which is generous, and you leave the inner door alone, which is wisdom.

hg_cursed_well.title: Cursed Well
hg_cursed_well.text:
A well, in a swamp — which is absurd, because there is water everywhere. Somebody dug down through all this wet ground looking for something cleaner, and found something else.

The rope is still on the winch. It is taut. Something is hanging on the other end of it.

choices.text: Leave the winch alone

outcome.text: The rope stays taut behind you for as long as you can see the well.

choices.text: Turn the winch and see what comes up

outcome.text: It comes up easily. It comes up much too easily, in fact, for the weight that was on the rope.

choices.text: Cut the rope and let whatever it is go back down

outcome.text: You can feel it up the rope like a pulse — patient, attentive, entirely aware that someone has come. You cut the rope near the winch and the tension goes out of it, and something a long way down makes a sound of what is unmistakably disappointment. Then nothing. You fill the shaft with stones for an hour to be certain.

choices.text: Purify the shaft

outcome.text: You work the rite down the shaft in stages, and what is on the rope comes apart quietly on the way up — not destroyed, released, the way a knot is released. What finally reaches the top is a bucket. In the bucket is clean water, the first you have seen in this realm, and it tastes of nothing at all, which is extraordinary.

hg_preta_feast_swamp.title: Preta Feast
hg_preta_feast_swamp.text:
They have laid a table in the marsh. A real table, on real trestles, in eight inches of standing water — and on it, a banquet: rice, fruit, roast meat, all of it steaming.

The pretas are seated around it. None of them is eating. They are all just looking at it, and have been for a long time.

choices.text: Walk on past the table

outcome.text: Nobody at the table looks up as you go. The food is still steaming when you lose sight of it.

choices.text: Sit down and eat

outcome.text: It is real, and it is good, and it is the best meal you have had in weeks. Every preta at the table watches every mouthful. Nobody stops you. Nobody says anything. You finish because stopping halfway would somehow be worse.

choices.text: Take a bowl and feed the nearest one by hand

outcome.text: The throat is the width of a straw and the swallowing has to be taught — small, slow, wait, again. It takes twenty minutes to get four mouthfuls into her. She keeps them down. The others watch this happen with an attention that is difficult to be the subject of. When you leave, three of them have moved their chairs closer to hers.

choices.text: Look at what is actually on the table first.

outcome.text:
You look, and having looked you decline, and the declining is easy in a way it has not been easy for years.

The pretas cannot make you want it. They have nothing else to offer and drift off to find someone who can be worked with.

choices.text: Ask why nobody is eating

outcome.text: "Because it will end," says the one at the head of the table, without looking away from the rice. "While we do not begin, it is still whole." You sit with that for a while. Then you point out, gently, that the food is going cold, and that this is also an ending, and that it is happening whether or not anyone begins. There is a very long silence. Then somebody picks up a spoon.

hg_medicinal_garden.title: Medicinal Garden
hg_medicinal_garden.text:
Something is growing here on purpose. Beds of herbs in ordered rows, staked and labelled, tended in a place where nothing should tend anything — and the labels are in a careful hand, in a language you half-recognise.

A preserved one straightens up from the weeding and regards you without alarm. "Patients or customers?"

choices.text: Customers

outcome.text: She lays out what is dried and ready, and prices it fairly.

choices.text: Neither — apologise for the intrusion

outcome.text: "Mm," she says, and goes back to the weeding. "Mind the third bed."

choices.text: Offer your hands for the afternoon

outcome.text: She sets you thinning the third bed and does not explain why it matters until you have done it correctly, at which point she explains at length and with real pleasure. Nothing grows well in this realm; everything here grows because she made it. You leave with your kit restocked and an open invitation.

choices.text: Ask for the thing that helps rather than the thing that cures.

outcome.text:
The gardener stops what she is doing. It is, apparently, a much rarer request than the other one and a considerably easier one to fulfil.

What she gives you will not fix anything. It makes tomorrow's walking possible, which is the whole of what you asked for.

choices.text: Ask about the beds she has not mentioned.

outcome.text:
She has not mentioned them because most people do not ask, and most people who do ask are not asking about medicine.

She establishes which you are with one question, and appears satisfied with the answer.

choices.text: Ask how anything grows in the realm of hunger

outcome.text: "It doesn't," she says. "I feed it." She shows you the trench at the garden's edge, where she has been composting her own substance — a little at a time, for a very long time, into the soil. She is markedly less than she was when she started. She considers this an entirely reasonable arrangement and will not be argued with.

hg_graveyard_dog.title: Grave Hound
hg_graveyard_dog.text:
It is standing on a grave mound with its head down and its green eyes fixed on you, and it has not decided yet. A grave hound alone is a guard; a grave hound in a pack is a problem. This one is alone.

Behind it, the mound has been dug at. Not by the hound.

choices.text: Put it down
Throw it food and go around

outcome.text: It takes the meat back onto the mound and eats there, watching you the whole time, guarding even while it chews.

choices.text: Look at what dug the mound

outcome.text: Tool marks, not claws — somebody came for this grave with a spade and left in a hurry. The hound is not guarding the grave from you; it is guarding it from whoever is coming back. You reset the turf and stack stones over it while the hound watches, and when you finish it lies down. It is still lying there when you look back.

choices.text: It is a dog. You are going to do this whatever anyone says.

outcome.text:
It is a dog in the way that a burnt-out house is a house, and you go toward it anyway with your hand out, and the party makes noises.

It lets you. It has apparently been standing on that grave for a very long time and nobody has offered it anything since.

choices.text: Speak to it the way you would to a working dog

outcome.text: Low voice, no eye contact, hand held out flat and still. Whatever it is now, it was a dog once, and something in the shape of the address gets through. It comes down off the mound and walks you a quarter mile to the graveyard's edge, and turns back at the boundary of what it considers its ground.

hg_skeleton_army.title: Skeleton Army
hg_skeleton_army.text:
They are drawn up in ranks across the whole width of the dry valley, and they are not moving. Rank on rank of skeleton infantry in the armour of an army that lost — you can tell it lost, because it is all still here.

They are facing an enemy that is no longer present. They have been facing it for a very long time.

choices.text: Go around the flank, quietly

outcome.text: Two hours of picking along the valley wall while ten thousand skulls face resolutely the other way. Not one of them turns.

choices.text: Walk straight through the ranks

outcome.text: You are six ranks deep when the nearest one registers that something has entered the formation, and the correction ripples outward.

choices.text: Give the order to stand down

outcome.text: You walk to the front, face the ranks, and dismiss them — properly, with the form and the cadence, the way it is done at the end of a campaign. It takes a moment. Then ten thousand skeletons ground their arms in one enormous rattling crash and the formation simply ceases to be a formation. Some of them sit down. Most of them come apart. What is left is a valley full of bones and a great deal of abandoned equipment.

choices.text: Work out what they are still facing

outcome.text: The line is anchored on high ground at both ends and refused on the left — a textbook defensive deployment against cavalry that would have come from the north. There is no north army. There has not been for centuries. But there is a supply train behind the line, unlooted, because nobody has ever gotten past the ranks to it.

hg_ancient_crypt.title: Ancient Crypt
hg_ancient_crypt.text:
The crypt door is stone, and it is ajar — about a hand's width, which is both an invitation and a warning depending on which side of it opened.

Dry air comes out. It smells of dust and cold iron and nothing organic at all.

choices.text: Pull the door to and walk away

outcome.text: The stone grinds shut. It takes both hands and most of your weight, and it feels like the right thing to have done.

choices.text: Go in

outcome.text: Two of them are standing just inside the door, one to each side, in the dark. They have been standing there since the door was last closed.

on_victory.text: Past the door-guards, the crypt is undisturbed and generously furnished.

choices.text: Listen at the gap before you open it

outcome.text: Nothing breathes in there, but something *shifts* — twice, at an interval, the way a person shifts weight when they have been standing a long time. Two of them, flanking the door. You open it wide instead of squeezing through, and take them from outside with the light behind you, which turns a bad fight into a short one.

choices.text: Read the door before touching it

outcome.text: The inscription is a service contract. The two inside are not guardians in any hostile sense — they are staff, on a term of duty that expired four hundred years ago because the family that hired them stopped existing. You go in and tell them so. There is a pause you would describe as stunned. Then they hand over the keys, formally, and lie down in the alcoves they were meant to occupy in the first place.

hg_crumbling_mausoleum.title: Crumbling Mausoleum
